2027-05-27.title: Second Thursday of the Apostles: the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ
2027-05-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Melchizedek brings out bread and wine
A pure offering in every place
This is my body that is for you
My flesh is true food and my blood is true drink
2027-05-27.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ is a Feast of Our Lord; the Syro-Malabar Church keeps it on the Thursday after the Feast of the Holy Trinity. The calendar notes the fuller passages: Genesis 14:1–20; Malachi 1:6–12; 1 Corinthians 10:15–17 with 11:23–30; John 6:51–64. In India the Latin Church keeps the solemnity of Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May (verify locally for parish processions and adoration).
2027-05-27.verse: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
theo: Two months after Easter, and eleven days after Pentecost, the Church stops on a Thursday to adore the gift that Jesus left on another Thursday, the night before he died. On Maundy Thursday the joy of the gift was overshadowed by the betrayal and the Passion. Today, in the Season of the Apostles, the Church celebrates the same gift in full light: the Body and Blood of Christ, given in every Holy Qurbana from the Upper Room to our own parish altar. The apostles, filled with the Spirit, did not only preach; they broke bread. The first believers “devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42). The Church that the apostles founded has been a Eucharistic Church from the first day. Our own Mar Thoma Christians received this faith from the apostle Thomas, and the word we use for the Eucharist, Qurbana, a Syriac word for offering or sacrifice, says what it is: the offering of Christ himself.

The first reading takes us back almost two thousand years before Christ. Abram returns from battle, having rescued his nephew Lot, and a mysterious figure comes out to meet him: “And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.” He blesses Abram: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand!” Melchizedek appears and disappears in three verses, yet the Bible never forgets him. The psalm says of the coming Messiah: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Psalm 110:4), and the Letter to the Hebrews sees in him an image of Christ, “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever” (Hebrews 7:3). A king of peace and righteousness, a priest who offers bread and wine: the Church has always seen here the first outline of the Eucharist. At the altar our priest still offers bread and wine, and they become the Body and Blood of the eternal High Priest.

The second reading is a hard word to priests. Through the prophet Malachi God complains that the priests of the restored Temple are offering blind, lame and sick animals, the leftovers of the flock: “By offering polluted food on my altar. And you say, ‘How have we polluted it?’ By thinking that the Lord’s table may be despised.” God would rather the Temple doors were shut than that worship should continue carelessly. Then comes a promise that reaches far beyond Jerusalem: “For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts.” From the earliest centuries Christians read this verse as a prophecy of the Eucharist. The Didache, one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament, applies it to the Sunday breaking of bread, and St Justin and St Irenaeus did the same. Today, at every hour, somewhere from the rising of the sun to its setting, the Holy Qurbana is being offered, in Kerala and in Chicago, in Rome and in a forest chapel in Arunachal: one pure offering, Christ himself. Malachi's warning remains for us too. We can despise the Lord's table by arriving late and leaving early, by careless dress and wandering eyes, by giving God the leftovers of our Sunday.

In the Epistle Paul hands on the oldest written account of the Last Supper, written about twenty-five years after the event: “For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, ‘This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.’” Received and handed on: this is what tradition means. Paul did not invent the Eucharist; he passed on what the Church already did. And he draws a serious conclusion: “For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes. Whoever, therefore, eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be answerable for the body and blood of the Lord. Examine yourselves, and only then eat of the bread and drink of the cup.” The Corinthians were sharing the Lord's Supper while the rich ate well and the poor went hungry. To fail to discern the Body, Paul says, is to fail to see both Christ truly present in the sacrament and Christ present in the brothers and sisters gathered around it. That is why the Church asks us to confess serious sins before receiving, to keep the Eucharistic fast, and to come to Communion reconciled with our neighbour.

The Gospel is the heart of the discourse in Capernaum: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.” His hearers dispute: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” Jesus does not soften his words. He makes them stronger: “Very truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood have eternal life, and I will raise them up on the last day; for my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.” True food, true drink: not a symbol only, not a pious memory, but the real Christ. This is what the Catholic Church believes and what the Council of Trent called transubstantiation: at the consecration the whole substance of the bread becomes the Body of Christ and the whole substance of the wine his Blood, while the appearances remain. And the purpose of it all is communion: “Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.” Whoever receives the Lord worthily carries him out into the street, the office, the kitchen and the hospital ward. Many of our parishes will carry the Blessed Sacrament in procession in these days, under the umbrellas and through the lanes, with children scattering petals. It is the same mystery: Christ who comes to us in the Qurbana wants to go with us wherever we live.
conn: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Psalm 110:4); Jesus has entered the sanctuary as “a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek” (Hebrews 6:20).
Malachi 1:11 is applied to the Eucharist in the Didache (chapter 14) and by St Justin and St Irenaeus; the Church sees it fulfilled when Christ offers himself through the priest in every place.
“It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat” (Exodus 16:15); “Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died” (John 6:49).
“Take; this is my body.” “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many” (Mark 14:22, 24).
“He took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him” (Luke 24:30–31).
“The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body” (1 Corinthians 10:16–17).
“I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord” (Psalm 116:13).
altar: At the consecration the priest repeats the words of the Lord, “This is my body… this is my blood”, and by the power of the Holy Spirit, whom we invoke in the epiclesis of our anaphora, the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ. What Melchizedek foreshadowed and Malachi foretold is placed on our altar.

When we receive Holy Communion, the Lord says to each one what he said in Capernaum: whoever eats me will live because of me. Let us receive him with a clean heart, and carry him out of the church into our homes and streets.
outline: From the Upper Room to our parish altar: a Thursday of thanksgiving in the Season of the Apostles.
Point 1 · Bread and wine of Melchizedek
Point 2 · A pure offering in every place
The words of institution and the call to examine ourselves.
Point 4 · True food and true drink

live: Before your next Communion, examine your conscience; if there is serious sin, go first to confession.
Do not despise the Lord's table (Malachi 1:7)
Come early to the Qurbana this Sunday, dress with reverence, and stay to the end and for a moment of thanks.
Spend fifteen minutes this week before the Blessed Sacrament, in adoration or in a visit to the church.
Take part in a Eucharistic procession or adoration in your parish, and bring a child or an elderly person with you.
fathers: In your bread is hidden the Spirit who is not consumed; in your wine dwells the fire that is not drunk. The Spirit in your bread, the fire in your wine: a wonder heard from our own lips.

Do not regard the bread and wine as plain bread and wine, for they are the Body and Blood of Christ, as the Lord himself declared. Even if the senses suggest otherwise, let faith make you firm. Do not judge by taste, but be fully assured by faith.

We do not receive these as common bread and common drink. As Jesus Christ our Saviour was made flesh by the Word of God, so we have been taught that the food over which thanks has been given by his word is the flesh and blood of that same Jesus who was made flesh.
magis: At the heart of the Eucharistic celebration are the bread and wine that become the Body and Blood of Christ; the Church sees in the gesture of Melchizedek, who brought out bread and wine, a prefiguring of her own offering.
The Eucharist is called the Holy Sacrifice because it makes present the one sacrifice of Christ; it is also called the pure and holy sacrifice.
In the most blessed sacrament the Body and Blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and therefore the whole Christ, is truly, really and substantially contained.

The Council of Trent: by the consecration the whole substance of bread is changed into the substance of the Body of Christ and the whole substance of wine into the substance of his Blood; this change the Church has fittingly called transubstantiation.
To respond to this invitation we must prepare ourselves; anyone conscious of a grave sin must receive the sacrament of Reconciliation before coming to Communion (1 Corinthians 11:27–29).
St John Paul II, Ecclesia de Eucharistia 1
The Church draws her life from the Eucharist.
saints: The Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ in the Syro-Malabar calendar. In the Latin calendar, St Augustine of Canterbury; the Latin Church in India keeps Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May.

26–31 May: second and third weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Wed 26: in the Latin calendar, St Philip Neri. Thu 27: the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ (the Latin Church in India keeps Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May). Sat 29: in the Latin calendar, St Paul VI. Sun 30: Third Sunday of the Apostles. Mon 31: the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which closes the month of Mary. The Sacred Heart of Jesus falls on Friday 4 June.
2027-05-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek, on the night you were betrayed you took bread and wine and gave us your Body and Blood. We adore you truly present in the Holy Qurbana, offered from the rising of the sun to its setting. Give us hearts that discern your Body, in the sacrament and in our brothers and sisters. Let us never despise your table, but come to it cleansed and grateful. Feed us with the living bread, that we may abide in you and you in us, and raise us up on the last day. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.

2027-05-27.question: Do I come to the Holy Qurbana as to the true Body and Blood of the Lord?
catechism: Melchizedek and the bread and wine.
kidsaint: Carlo was an Italian boy who loved computers, football and his dog. Most of all he loved Jesus in the Holy Qurbana. He went to Mass every day he could, and he made a website about Eucharistic miracles from around the world. He used to say that the Eucharist was his highway to heaven. Carlo died of leukaemia in 2006 when he was fifteen, and Pope Leo XIV declared him a saint in 2025. Lesson: you are never too young to love Jesus in the Eucharist!
2027-05-27.special: Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ (Syro-Malabar, Thursday). Latin Church in India: Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May.
term: The Syriac word for offering or sacrifice, used by the Syro-Malabar Church for the Eucharistic celebration, the Holy Qurbana. The solemn form celebrated on great occasions is called Raza, the Mystery. The word says what the Church believes: the Qurbana is the sacrifice of Christ made present, and the Body and Blood of the Lord given to the faithful.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had supper with his friends. He took bread and said, “This is my body that is for you.” He took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” Every time the priest says these words at the Holy Qurbana, the bread and wine become Jesus himself. It still looks like bread, but it is Jesus. That is why we kneel, we are quiet, and we receive him with clean hearts.
family.intention: We pray for children preparing for their First Holy Communion, and for those who are sick and cannot come to church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get ready at home on Saturday for the Holy Qurbana on Sunday?”

illus: A retired schoolteacher in a village near Changanassery could no longer walk to church after a stroke. Every Sunday a young deacon brought Holy Communion to her house. Her grandson, who had stopped going to church, noticed that every Saturday evening his grandmother asked him to sweep the front room, put a white cloth on the small table, place a candle and a crucifix on it, and help her into a clean sari. One Saturday he asked her, a little impatiently, why she made such a fuss for a few minutes' visit. She said, ‘Because the King is coming to my house.’ The next morning, when the deacon arrived, the grandson found that he was kneeling beside her without having planned to. ‘I had heard the word Real Presence a hundred times in catechism,’ he said later. ‘I understood it in my grandmother's front room.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, truly present in the Holy Qurbana, we adore you and we thank you. Gather us now around your word and make our hearts ready to receive you. Amen.
share: Melchizedek brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18). What does it mean to me that Christ is a priest forever?
By thinking that the Lord's table may be despised (Malachi 1:7). Have I given God only my leftovers?
Examine yourselves, and only then eat of the bread (1 Corinthians 11:28). How do I prepare for Holy Communion?
Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them (John 6:56). Where do I carry the Lord after I receive him?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the living bread: give us life.
interc: For the Church, that she may always draw her life from the Eucharist and offer the pure offering in every place.
For our priests, that they may celebrate the Holy Qurbana with faith and reverence.
For children preparing for First Holy Communion and for their families.
For the sick and the housebound, that they may receive the Lord in their homes.
For the hungry of the world, that those who share the one bread may share their bread with the poor.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave us his Body and Blood as true food and true drink. Make us discern his Body in the sacrament and in our neighbour, abide in him always, and come at last to the banquet of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Church does what she did on Maundy Thursday, but now in the full light of Easter and Pentecost: she gives thanks for the Body and Blood of Christ. The word Qurbana means offering. In every Qurbana Christ offers himself, and gives himself to us.

Long before Christ, a king and priest named Melchizedek came out to meet Abram with bread and wine and blessed him. The Bible calls Jesus a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek. At our altar too, bread and wine are offered, and they become the Body and Blood of the eternal Priest.

Through Malachi God complains about careless worship: blind and lame animals, the leftovers. But he promises: from the rising of the sun to its setting, a pure offering will be made to my name in every place (Malachi 1:11). The first Christians saw here the Eucharist, offered every hour somewhere in the world. Let us never give God our leftovers.

Paul hands on what he received: on the night he was betrayed, Jesus took bread and said, “This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” Then Paul warns: examine yourselves, and only then eat (1 Corinthians 11:24, 28). Let us come to Communion with a clean heart, reconciled with God and with our neighbour.

In the Gospel Jesus says: my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink (John 6:55). Not only a sign, but truly himself. It looks like bread, but it is the Lord. That is why we kneel, we fast before Communion, we keep silence, and we adore him.

And Jesus says: whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in them (John 6:56). We carry him out of the church. In these days many of our parishes walk in procession with the Blessed Sacrament. Let our whole life be such a procession, carrying Christ to our homes and streets. Amen.
kids: Children, at the Holy Qurbana the priest says the words of Jesus: “This is my body.” Then the bread becomes Jesus himself! It still looks like bread, but it is Jesus.
That is why we are quiet and we kneel. When you see the priest lift up the Host, say softly in your heart: “My Lord and my God!”

opts.a: Lord, to whom can we go?
intro: When Jesus said, my flesh is true food, many disciples left him. He did not call them back with a softer teaching. He asked the Twelve: do you also wish to go away?

sub: Israel fed in the desert.
Your ancestors ate and died.
Whoever eats this bread will live forever.

opts.resolve: This week I will spend time before the Blessed Sacrament and say: Lord, to whom can we go?
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in today's Gospel Jesus says: this is the bread that came down from heaven, not like that which your ancestors ate, and they died. But the one who eats this bread will live forever (John 6:58). In the desert God fed Israel with manna each morning. It sustained their bodies for a time. The bread Christ gives is himself, and it gives eternal life.

But the Gospel goes on. When many of his disciples heard it, they said: this teaching is difficult; who can accept it? (John 6:60). And many turned back and no longer went about with him. Notice: Jesus did not call them back and say, I only meant a symbol. He let them go, because he had spoken the truth. The bread is truly his flesh; the cup is truly his blood.

Then he turned to the Twelve and asked: do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). It is like Joshua's challenge to Israel: choose this day whom you will serve (Joshua 24:15). Today many people, even baptised Christians, find the mystery of the Eucharist too hard. The question comes to each of us: will I stay?

Simon Peter answered: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God (John 6:68–69). Peter did not understand everything. But he knew Jesus, and he trusted him. The Psalm invites us: O taste and see that the LORD is good (Psalm 34:8).

On this Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, let us learn what the Church teaches and share it with our children. Let us spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this week. And when we receive him at the Holy Qurbana, let us say with Peter: Lord, to whom can we go? Amen.

intro: The Eucharist is not only Christ given to each of us. It makes us one body. Paul warns that a Communion which forgets the poor brother does not discern the body.

points.h: We who are many are one body
sub: The cup of blessing.
One bread, one body.
Unity as the fruit of Communion.
points.apply: Pray after Communion for the person sitting next to you.

homily: Dear friends, Paul asks the Corinthians: the cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread (1 Corinthians 10:16–17).

The Eucharist does two things at once. It gives us Christ, truly present, Body and Blood, soul and divinity. And it makes us one body in him. Saint Augustine told his people: receive what you are, the Body of Christ. The Psalm says: how very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity (Psalm 133:1). After Communion, let us pray for the person beside us.

But in Corinth something was wrong. When they gathered for the Lord's supper, the rich ate first and the poor went hungry (1 Corinthians 11:21). Paul said: that is not really to eat the Lord's supper. And he warned that all who eat and drink without discerning the body eat and drink judgment against themselves (1 Corinthians 11:29). Amos had condemned those who lay on beds of ivory and were not grieved over the ruin of their people (Amos 6:4–6). To discern the body is to see Christ in the bread, and also in the poor brother at the door.

In these days many of our parishes carry the Blessed Sacrament in procession. David danced before the ark of the LORD as it was brought into the city (2 Samuel 6:14). At Emmaus the two disciples recognised the Lord in the breaking of the bread, and their hearts burned (Luke 24:30–32). The procession shows that Christ does not stay locked in the church. He walks with his people.

So let us come to the Holy Qurbana as one family. Let us pray for our neighbour after Communion. Let us share a meal this week with someone poor or lonely. And let us walk behind the Blessed Sacrament, carrying the Lord into our homes and streets. Amen.

intro: Theme: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”
On the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ: the bread and wine of Melchizedek, the pure offering foretold by Malachi, the tradition handed on by Paul, and the true food and drink of the Gospel.

sub: A priest-king who comes from nowhere.
Blessing in the name of God Most High.
A priest forever.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
points.apply: Pray this week for your parish priest and for vocations to the priesthood.

points.h: A pure offering in every place
sub: The leftovers on the altar.
Better to shut the doors than to worship carelessly.
From the rising of the sun to its setting.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts.
And it is by God’s will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
points.apply: Come early to the Sunday Qurbana, and stay to the end with a moment of thanksgiving.

sub: The night he was betrayed.
Do this in remembrance of me.
Examine yourselves and discern the Body.
q: This day shall be a day of remembrance for you. You shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord; throughout your generations you shall observe it as a perpetual ordinance.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
points.apply: Before your next Communion, examine your conscience and, if needed, go to confession.

sub: How can this man give us his flesh?
Unless you eat, you have no life.
Abiding in him, carrying him out.
q: When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes in adoration this week, or join the Eucharistic procession of your parish.

concl: The priest of Melchizedek's order offers himself in every place: the Holy Qurbana is the pure offering and the true food of the Church.
Let us discern his Body, come to him with clean hearts, and carry him into our homes and streets.
